sections.title: What Is a Token?
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     WHAT IS A TOKEN?                            │
│                                                                 │
│  A token is a CHUNK of text — the smallest unit an LLM sees.   │
│  NOT always a word. Can be part of a word, a symbol, a space.  │
│                                                                 │
│  EXAMPLES (GPT tokenizer):                                      │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │  "cat"           →  ["cat"]              = 1 token     │    │
│  │  "cats"          →  ["cats"]             = 1 token     │    │
│  │  "caterpillar"   →  ["cat","erpillar"]   = 2 tokens    │    │
│  │  "ChatGPT"       →  ["Chat","GPT"]       = 2 tokens    │    │
│  │  "indubitably"   →  ["ind","ub","itably"]= 3 tokens    │    │
│  │  "Hello, world!" →  ["Hello",","," world","!"]= 4 tok  │    │
│  │  " Python"       →  [" Python"]          = 1 token     │    │
│  │  "Python"        →  ["Python"]           = 1 token     │    │
│  │  NOTE: space before word = different token!             │    │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                 │
│  THE GOLDEN RULE:                                               │
│  Common words    → 1 token                                      │
│  Rare/long words → multiple tokens                              │
│  Numbers         → 1 digit per token often                      │
│  Code            → often more tokens than English               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
